idiom_name: the TestCase (or one of its bound methods) passed as the collaborator, via duck typing
implementation_notes: Python collaborators are protocols in the typing sense, not declarations: any object with the expected attribute satisfies the SUT, so the test object can implement the callback as a method and pass self (or self.on_event) into the constructor or registration call, with the recorded values read by the test method. unittest creates a fresh TestCase instance per test method, so the observation state stays per-test; passing a bound method keeps it attached to that instance. When the collaborator is a plain callable, a local function or lambda capturing test variables is the lighter form, and unittest.mock.Mock with assert_called_once_with replaces the hand-written shunt as soon as call cardinality or argument matching has to be asserted.
code_sketch:
class PublisherTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def on_event(self, e):                 # the test object is the collaborator
        self.seen.append(e)

    def test_publishes_once(self):
        self.seen = []
        publisher = Publisher(self.on_event)      # duck-typed install
        publisher.change("x")
        self.assertEqual(["x"], self.seen)
pitfalls: A bound method handed to a long-lived subject keeps the TestCase alive after the test, so a late callback mutates a finished test's state; unregister or re-create the subject per test.
unittest creates a new test instance per method, but pytest classes and module-level subjects are shared, so recording attributes initialised once leak between tests.

The shunt has no built-in expectation check: a callback that never fired looks the same as one that fired zero times, so assert the recorded list explicitly (or count calls) rather than relying on the callback.
